verdicts.text: Requires at least four outcomes, implies a 160-character limit, and provides a prerequisite-copy example but no measurable-outcome example.
Explains objective choices, prompts authors to define success, and offers AI improvement beside percentage progress.
AI generates a reviewable course outline, while contextual suggestions target marketing copy rather than measurable outcomes.
An AI assistant is present in lesson editing, but its prompts and objective-related behavior are not visible.
Generic writing and social-caption generation do not evidence learning-objective authoring guidance.

reject.reason: Generic Magic Write task presets are too distant from course-objective authoring.
Generated Instagram captions and refinement controls do not address measurable learning outcomes.

takeCorrections.take: Udemy requires at least four separate outcomes; the displayed numbers are remaining-character counters implying a 160-character maximum.
Udemy provides an explicit prerequisite placeholder example, but it does not model a measurable learning outcome.
Kajabi generates editable course structure and descriptions for review, not demonstrated learning objectives.
Ama's visible suggestions concern opt-in and sales copy, not course-objective authoring.
The capture shows selected lesson text and a color picker with an AI button present; it does not demonstrate AI editing behavior.

counterCandidates.reason: A course-specific AI generator can still stop at topic-to-outline generation without coaching measurable outcomes.
Placing AI at the authoring surface does not establish objective-specific prompts, examples, or quality checks.
